transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a customer order for 1800 cartons of the new 750-milliliter format due by Monday morning, and Line 6 is available for a Saturday shift. I understand the new format has completed a dry fit on Line 6, but no production run has been authorized yet. That decision is mine to make. Before I can authorize anything, I need to go through our normal Saturday startup routine — quality, maintenance, and safety each need to report and formally record any findings. I'd like to hear from each of you on where things stand so we can determine whether this run can proceed, and if so, under what conditions. Let's start with the current status of Line 6 and the new format.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important from my quality review. I completed my review of the new-format trial paperwork yesterday, and it shows that the first production run requires a 30-minute first-article approval and 100% inspection of the first 200 cartons. The paperwork is currently still in quality's unfiled trial folder, but the findings are clear: we need to plan for that first-article approval and full inspection of the first 200 cartons before we can proceed with full production.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a critical maintenance finding. I confirmed from the installed servo controller's latest firmware record — which I received from the vendor this morning — that the new 750-milliliter format must run at exactly 90 cartons per minute or slower on Line 6. Additionally, the format changeover requires 2 hours of mechanical setup. I should note that the maintenance work order for this has not yet been opened, so we need to get that created and track the setup time in our planning.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: During my safety walkdown yesterday, I documented a critical finding for the new 750-milliliter format on Line 6. The new-format guide adjustment requires two trained employees during setup, and a marked 1.5-meter exclusion zone must be established around the infeed. I recorded this finding during yesterday's walkdown, but I want to flag that the Saturday startup board has not yet been updated with this information, so it needs to be formally entered now.
transcript.speaker: A4
